own_solution.law: P = F·v = Fv cos(theta). The base power is 120 cos(30°) = 103.923 W. For an additional tilt q of the pulling rope, P = 120 cos(30° + q), giving 89.1774 W, 81.8398 W and 70.5342 W at q = 12°, 17° and 24°, respectively.
assumptions: The sled moves horizontally along the level ground.
The pulling force acts along the rope.
The stated tension and speed remain fixed when the pulling rope is tilted, as explicitly specified.
Power is evaluated at the resulting rope angle.

TF8CB.regime: F < q: the 40 N tension is below every listed rope strength.

T8FA9.regime: F < q: the 40 N tension is below every listed breaking threshold.

notes: All certified answers at all listed values agree with the governing relation and appropriate rounding. Duration cancels through P = (F cos(theta) v t)/t for all listed positive durations. The second sled and the earlier trial have no stated physical path to the present power. All listed rope strengths exceed 40 N; the outside-regime reference is not needed to certify these cases.
